summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (JTM 5.3/20)

data.turoyo: zox aḥuno xayifo manhər annaqqe. hol d aṯi maqəṯle u šamʕayḏe w rayəḥ w ǧeye, nahər.
data.translation: Geh rasch, Bruder, und lass es nun tagen. Bis er kam und seine Kerze anzündete und so weiter, da wurde es Tag.

summary: New sense 2: leuchten, Licht geben (von einer Lampe)

summary: Restore the accusative ending in “seinen Stern”.
rationale: Stern is the accusative object of aufgehen lassen. The supplied edition translation reads “ohne daß Gott seinen Stern hätte aufgehen lassen”. The current sein omits the case ending.

summary: I.1 is overwhelmingly an impersonal dawn predicate; ṣafro/yawmo may be overt. ʕal marks those overtaken by dawn, not an agent or experiencer-coded argument requiring a new sense.
Preterit Intransitive narrates completed onset. ko-Infectum, g-/gəd-Infectum, and unprefixed temporal complements retain their own discourse roles; German past tense does not determine the box.

III.1 already contains literal room illumination, a radiant face, devotional light and the star/son metaphor; preserve its mixed inherited gloss, including the existing editorial remark. III.2 is deliberate daybreak control, not another metaphorical son sense.
Part act. nahərto with fayišo and a long temporal span supports sustained lamp light (I.2). German brannte is not evidence for consuming or burning something.
Verify nahərto vocalization at Talay 2/25, while retaining its clearly lamp-light interpretation.
Check Nahe versus existing nahər at 29/123; do not silently correct the source. At MAC MuA Quzko/28, dawn followed by at night may be a restart.

PrS 16/21 German stops before the dawn clause (reportedly continued in v.22); PrS 75/82 omits both dawn-dispute tokens. 96/172 has German Nacht where Turoyo has Nahər: verify edition segmentation and wording before quotation.
Reader’s already-cited claim for 47/27 is not supported by the supplied nhr entry; no entry citation correction inferred from that claim.
The III.1 inherited leuchten gloss underrepresents the transitive literal examples, but retain it pending editorial discussion rather than deleting the existing remark.
Correct “Lich” to “Licht”.
rationale: Lich is missing the final t of the German noun Licht, translating u=nuhrayḏux.

summary: Correct “Totenraiches” to “Totenreiches”.
rationale: The German genitive of Totenreich is Totenreiches; raich is a spelling error.
